title: Bekhorot 5
description: Rabbi Elazar’s dream settles Rabbi Yoḥanan’s reason, Rav Mordekhai reverses the dispute, Kontrokos the officer tests Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai on the Levites’ count and Moses’ silver, Rav Ḥisda finds the doubled Sanctuary maneh in Ezekiel, Rabbi Eliezer explains donkeys, Rephidim and Shittim, and a new mishna rules on a cow that bears a donkey and a donkey that bears a horse.

🪙 201 talents collected, 100 given: the Sanctuary maneh was double
⚖️ Rav Ḥisda and Ezekiel’s sixty-shekel maneh: add up to a sixth, from the outside

a2.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, כִּדְאָמַר טַעַם, אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן — מַאי טַעְמָא?

a3.he: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן חֲזַאי בְּחֶילְמָא דְּמִילְּתָא מְעַלַּיְתָא אָמֵינָא, אָמַר קְרָא ״לִי יִהְיוּ״ — בַּהֲוָיָיתָן יְהוּ.

a4.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, ״וְהָיָה כִּי יְבִיאֲךָ... וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ? הַהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתָנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: עֲשֵׂה מִצְוָה זוֹ שֶׁבִּשְׁבִילָהּ תִּיכָּנֵס לָאָרֶץ.

a5.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מָרְדֳּכַי לְרַב אָשֵׁי: אַתּוּן הָכִי מַתְנִיתוּ לַהּ, אֲנַן אִיפְּכָא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ, רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר, וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ אָמַר: קָדְשׁוּ בְּכוֹרוֹת בַּמִּדְבָּר.

a6.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְאָפְכִית נָמֵי תְּיוּבָתָא, וְאָפְכִיתוּ לַהּ לְהָא דְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: לֹא קָדְשׁוּ לְהוּ — לֹא הוּצְרְכוּ לִיקְדַּשׁ.

a7.he: אִי הָכִי, הַיְינוּ דִּידַן! קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן: חַיָּיב אָדָם לוֹמַר בִּלְשׁוֹן רַבּוֹ.

a8.he: שָׁאַל קוּנְטְרוּקוּס הַשַּׂר אֶת רַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי: בִּפְרָטָן שֶׁל לְוִיִּם אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁנַיִם אֶלֶף וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת, בִּכְלָלָן אַתָּה מוֹצֵא עֶשְׂרִים וּשְׁנַיִם אֶלֶף, וּשְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת לְהֵיכָן הָלְכוּ?

a9.he: אָמַר לוֹ: אוֹתָן שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת בְּכוֹרוֹת הָיוּ, וְאֵין בְּכוֹר מַפְקִיעַ בְּכוֹר. מַאי טַעְמָא? אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: דַּיּוֹ לַבְּכוֹר שֶׁיַּפְקִיעַ קְדוּשַּׁת עַצְמוֹ.

a10.he: וְעוֹד שְׁאָלוֹ: בְּגִיבּוּי כֶּסֶף אַתָּה מוֹצֵא מָאתַיִם וְאַחַת כִּכָּר וְאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מָנֶה, דִּכְתִיב: ״בֶּקַע לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת מַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְגוֹ׳״,

a11.he: וּבִנְתִינַת הַכֶּסֶף אַתָּה מוֹצֵא מְאַת כִּכָּר, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיְהִי מְאַת כִּכַּר הַכֶּסֶף לָצֶקֶת וְגוֹ׳״. מֹשֶׁה רַבְּכֶם גַּנָּב הָיָה, אוֹ קוּבְיוּסְטוּס הָיָה, אוֹ אֵינוֹ בָּקִי בְּחֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת? נָתַן מֶחֱצָה וְנָטַל מֶחֱצָה, וּמֶחֱצָה שָׁלֵם לֹא הֶחֱזִיר.

a12.he: אָמַר לוֹ: מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ גִּיזְבָּר נֶאֱמָן הָיָה, וּבָקִי בְּחֶשְׁבּוֹנוֹת הָיָה, וּמָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ כָּפוּל הָיָה.

a13.he: הָוֵי בַּהּ רַב אַחַאי: מַאי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ, ״וַיְהִי מְאַת כִּכַּר הַכֶּסֶף לָצֶקֶת וְגוֹ׳״? הָנָךְ לָצֶקֶת, וְאִינָךְ בֵּי גַזָּא! כְּתַב קְרָא אַחֲרִינָא: ״וְכֶסֶף פְּקוּדֵי הָעֵדָה מְאַת כִּכָּר וְגוֹ׳״.

a14.he: וּדְקָאָמַר לֵיהּ: מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ כָּפוּל הָיָה, מְנָא לֵיהּ?

a15.he: אִילֵימָא מִינֵּיהּ, שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּאן שִׁבְעִים וְאֶחָד מָנֶה — ״וְאֶת הָאָלֶף וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעִים עָשָׂה וָוִים לָעַמּוּדִים״, וְלֹא מְנָאָן הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא בִּפְרוֹטְרוֹט, וְאִם אִיתָא — מֵאָה וְאֶחָד כִּכָּר וְאַחַת עֶשְׂרֵה מָנֶה מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ!

a16.he: אֶלָּא, מִדְּלֹא מְנָאָן הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא בִּפְרוֹטְרוֹט, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ כָּפוּל הָיָה.

a17.he: וְדִילְמָא כְּלָלֵי קָחָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי, פְּרָטִי לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי!

a18.he: אֶלָּא מֵהָכָא: ״וּנְחֹשֶׁת הַתְּנוּפָה שִׁבְעִים כִּכָּר וְאַלְפַּיִם וְאַרְבַּע מֵאוֹת שָׁקֶל״, שֶׁהֲרֵי כָּאן תִּשְׁעִים וְשִׁשָּׁה מָנֶה, וְלֹא מְנָאָן הַכָּתוּב אֶלָּא בִּפְרוֹטְרוֹט, שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ כָּפוּל הָיָה.

a19.he: וְדִילְמָא פְּרָטָא רַבָּה קָא חָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי, פְּרָטָא זוּטָא לָא קָחָשֵׁיב בְּכַכְּרֵי!

a20.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מֵהָכָא, ״וְהַשֶּׁקֶל עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה עֶשְׂרִים שְׁקָלִים חֲמִשָּׁה וְעֶשְׂרִים שְׁקָלִים עֲשָׂרָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁקֶל הַמָּנֶה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם״.

b1.he: וְהָא מָאתַן וְאַרְבְּעִין הָוְיָין! אֶלָּא שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: מָנֶה שֶׁל קוֹדֶשׁ מָנֶה כָּפוּל הָיָה.

b2.he: וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ, מוֹסִיפִין עַל הַמִּדּוֹת, וְאֵין מוֹסִיפִין יָתֵר עַל שְׁתוּת, וּשְׁמַע מִינַּהּ שְׁתוּתָא מִלְּבַר.

b3.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: שָׁאַלְתִּי אֶת רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בְּבֵית מוֹתְבָא רַבָּא, מָה נִשְׁתַּנּוּ פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹרִים מִפִּטְרֵי סוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים? אָמַר לִי: גְּזֵירַת הַכָּתוּב הִיא, וְעוֹד שֶׁסִּיְּיעוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל בִּשְׁעַת יְצִיאָתָם מִמִּצְרַיִם, שֶׁאֵין לָךְ כׇּל אֶחָד וְאֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ עִמּוֹ תִּשְׁעִים חֲמוֹרִים לוּבִים טְעוּנִים מִכַּסְפָּהּ וּזְהָבָהּ שֶׁל מִצְרַיִם.

b4.he: וְעוֹד שְׁאִלְתִּיו: מַאי לְשׁוֹן ״רְפִידִים״? וְאָמַר לִי: רְפִידִים שְׁמָהּ. כְּתַנָּאֵי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: רְפִידִים שְׁמָהּ, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שֶׁרִיפּוּ עַצְמָן מִדִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה, וְכֵן הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״לֹא הִפְנוּ אָבוֹת אֶל בָּנִים מֵרִפְיוֹן יָדָיִם״.

b5.he: וְעוֹד שְׁאִלְתִּיו: מַאי לְשׁוֹן ״שִׁטִּים״? וְאָמַר לִי: שִׁטִּים שְׁמָהּ. כְּתַנָּאֵי: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: שִׁטִּים שְׁמָהּ, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שֶׁנִּתְעַסְקוּ בְּדִבְרֵי שְׁטוּת.

b6.he: ״וַתִּקְרֶאןָ לָעָם לְזִבְחֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶן״ — רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר: עֲרוּמּוֹת פָּגְעוּ בָּהֶן, רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: שֶׁנַּעֲשׂוּ כּוּלָּן בַּעֲלֵי קְרָיִין.

b7.he: מַתְנִי׳ פָּרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין חֲמוֹר, וַחֲמוֹר שֶׁיָּלְדָה כְּמִין סוּס — פְּטוּרָה מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר״ ״פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר״ שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים, עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הַיּוֹלֵד חֲמוֹר וְהַנּוֹלָד חֲמוֹר.

b8.he: וּמַה הֵם בַּאֲכִילָה? בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה טְמֵאָה — מוּתָּר בַּאֲכִילָה, וּטְמֵאָה שֶׁיָּלְדָה כְּמִין בְּהֵמָה טְהוֹרָה — אָסוּר בַּאֲכִילָה, שֶׁהַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַטָּמֵא — טָמֵא, וְהַיּוֹצֵא מִן הַטָּהוֹר — טָהוֹר.

b9.he: גְּמָ׳ תְּנַן הָתָם: רָחֵל שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין עֵז, וְעֵז שֶׁיָּלְדָה מִין רָחֵל — פָּטוּר מִן הַבְּכוֹרָה, וְאִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין — חַיָּיב.

b10.he: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי? אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר״ — שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר, ״בְּכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב״ — שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא כֶּשֶׂב וּבְכוֹרוֹ כֶּשֶׂב, ״בְּכוֹר עֵז״ — שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא עֵז וּבְכוֹרוֹ עֵז.

b11.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אַךְ״ — חִלֵּק.

b13.he: הוּא דְּאָמַר כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, דְּתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר: ״אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר״ — עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר, ״בְּכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב״ — עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא כֶּשֶׂב וּבְכוֹרוֹ כֶּשֶׂב, ״אוֹ בְכוֹר עֵז״ — עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא עֵז וּבְכוֹרוֹ עֵז.

b14.he: יָכוֹל אֲפִילּוּ יֵשׁ בּוֹ מִקְצָת סִימָנִין? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אַךְ״ — חִלֵּק.

b15.he: בְּמַאי קָמִיפַּלְגִי? תַּנָּא דִידַן סָבַר: גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא בִּקְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים, וְהוּא הַדִּין בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

b16.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סָבַר: גַּלִּי רַחֲמָנָא בִּקְדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף, וְהוּא הַדִּין בִּקְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים, וְגָמַר קְדוּשַּׁת דָּמִים מִקְּדוּשַּׁת הַגּוּף.

b17.he: וְתַנָּא דִידַן, הַאי ״בְּכוֹר״ ״בְּכוֹר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ? מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא.

b18.he: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: לָמָּה נֶאֶמְרוּ אֵימוּרִין בִּבְכוֹר שׁוֹר, אֵימוּרִין בִּבְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב, אֵימוּרִין בִּבְכוֹר עֵז?

b19.he: צְרִיכָא, דְּאִי כְּתַב רַחֲמָנָא בִּבְכוֹר שׁוֹר — שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבָּה בִּנְסָכִים.

b21.he: בְּעֵז — שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבָּה אֵצֶל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּיָחִיד.

b22.he: חֲדָא מֵחֲדָא לָא אָתְיָא, תֵּיתֵי חֲדָא מִתַּרְתֵּי!

b23.he: בְּהֵי לָא לִיכְתּוֹב? לָא לִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּשׁוֹר, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ — מָה לְהָנָךְ, שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבּוּ אֵצֶל פְּסָחִים!

b24.he: לָא לִכְתּוֹב בְּכֶשֶׂב, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ — מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן נִתְרַבּוּ אֵצֶל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בְּצִיבּוּר!

b25.he: לָא נִיכְתּוֹב רַחֲמָנָא בְּעֵז, וְתֵיתֵי מֵהָנָךְ — מָה לְהָנָךְ שֶׁכֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶן צַד רִבּוּי אֵצֶל מִזְבֵּחַ! הִילְכָּךְ צְרִיכִי.

b26.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, אִם כֵּן לִיכְתּוֹב קְרָא ״אַךְ בְּכוֹר שׁוֹר כֶּשֶׂב וְעֵז״, ״בְּכוֹר״ ״בְּכוֹר״ לְמָה לִי? אֶלָּא לָאו שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: עַד שֶׁיְּהֵא הוּא שׁוֹר וּבְכוֹרוֹ שׁוֹר.

b27.he: וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי, הַאי ״פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר״ ״פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר״ מַאי עָבֵיד לֵיהּ?

b28.he: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי אוֹמֵר, מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״אַךְ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה אֶת בְּכוֹר הָאָדָם וְאֵת בְּכוֹר הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה תִּפְדֶּה״, שׁוֹמֵעַ אֲנִי אֲפִילּוּ פִּטְרֵי סוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר״ — פֶּטֶר חֲמוֹר אָמַרְתִּי לְךָ, וְלֹא פִּטְרֵי סוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים.

b29.he: וַעֲדַיִין אֲנִי אוֹמֵר: פִּטְרֵי חֲמוֹר בְּשֶׂה, פִּטְרֵי סוּסִים וּגְמַלִּים בְּכׇל דָּבָר.

messages.text: 5a

Continued from 4b. Rav Pappa has restated the dispute about the firstborn born in the wilderness: “Rabbi Yoḥanan says they were sanctified and their sanctity did not cease, and Reish Lakish says they were sanctified only until the time of the census,”
Gemara
…and then their sanctity ceased following the census.

notes.he: משעת החשבון של חומש הפקודים ואילך:
notes.en: And their sanctity ceased: from the time of the census in the book of Numbers [Ḥumash HaPekudim] onward.

messages.text: Granted, according to Reish Lakish, who holds the firstborn were not sanctified following the census until they entered Eretz Yisrael, the reason is as he said, that it is written: “And it shall be when the Lord shall bring you into the land of the Canaanites…and you shall set apart all firstborn of the womb to the Lord” (Exodus 13:11–12).

verse.he: וְהָיָה כִּי־יְבִאֲךָ יְהֹוָה אֶל־אֶרֶץ הַכְּנַעֲנִי כַּאֲשֶׁר נִשְׁבַּע לְךָ וְלַאֲבֹתֶיךָ וּנְתָנָהּ לָךְ׃ וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ כׇל־פֶּטֶר־רֶחֶם לַיהֹוָה וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר ׀ שֶׁגֶר בְּהֵמָה אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה לְךָ הַזְּכָרִים לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: “And when GOD has brought you into the land of the Canaanites, as was sworn to you and to your fathers, and has given it to you, you shall set apart for GOD every first issue of the womb: every male firstling that your cattle drop shall be GOD’s.

notes.he: מוהיה כי יביאך והדר והעברת:
notes.en: His reason: from “And it shall be when He shall bring you,” and only then “and you shall set apart.”

notes.he: דאמר קדשו ופסקו כדקאמר טעמא דכניסתן לארץ ישראל קדשו בכורות אלמא דקדשו במדבר ופסקו:
notes.en: Granted, according to Reish Lakish: who said they were sanctified and then ceased. As he said, the reason is that the firstborn were sanctified [again] upon their entry into Eretz Yisrael; evidently they had been sanctified in the wilderness and then ceased.

messages.text: But according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, who holds that the firstborn continued to be sanctified following the census, what is the reason, i.e., the source, for his opinion?

notes.he: דאמר לא פסקו מאי טעמא:
notes.en: But according to Rabbi Yoḥanan: who said they did not cease, what is the reason?

messages.text: I saw Rabbi Yoḥanan in a dream, which is a sign that I am saying a proper matter in explaining his opinion. The verse states: “For all the firstborn are Mine: On the day that I smote all the firstborn in the land of Egypt I sanctified to Me all the firstborn in Israel, both man and animal, Mine they shall be: I am the Lord” (Numbers 3:13). The additional phrase “Mine they shall be” indicates that they shall be, i.e., shall remain, in their current state of sanctity.
messages.quote: what is the reason, i.e., the source, for his opinion

verse.he: כִּי לִי כׇּל־בְּכוֹר בְּיוֹם הַכֹּתִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם הִקְדַּשְׁתִּי לִי כׇל־בְּכוֹר בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל מֵאָדָם עַד־בְּהֵמָה לִי יִהְיוּ אֲנִי יְהֹוָה׃ {פ}
verse.en: For every such first-born is Mine: at the time that I smote every [male] first-born in the land of Egypt, I consecrated every first-born in Israel, human and animal, to Myself, to be Mine, GOD’s.

notes.he: ר' יוחנן חזאי בחילמא הילכ' מיסתייעא מילתא דמפרישנא טעמא שפיר אמר קרא והיו בהווייתן יהו דקדשו ולא פסקו:
notes.en: “I saw Rabbi Yoḥanan in a dream”: therefore the matter is supported, that I explain the reason well. The verse states “they shall be”: in their state they shall be, meaning they were sanctified and did not cease.

messages.text: And as for Rabbi Yoḥanan, with regard to the verse “And it shall be when the Lord shall bring you…and you shall set apart,” what does he do with it?
That expression is necessary to teach that which the tanna of the school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
Perform this mitzva on account of which you will be privileged to enter into Eretz Yisrael.

notes.he: של בכורות שבשבילה תיכנס לארץ ולהכי סמכינהו רחמנא להדדי:
notes.en: This mitzva: of the firstborn, on account of which you will enter the land; and that is why the Merciful One placed them next to each other.

notes.he: בזכות שתקיימה:
notes.en: On account of which you will enter the land: in the merit of fulfilling it.

messages.text: @Rav Ashi You teach the dispute between Rabbi Yoḥanan and Reish Lakish in this manner, whereas we teach it in the opposite manner: Rabbi Yoḥanan says the firstborn were not sanctified in the wilderness, and Reish Lakish says the firstborn were sanctified in the wilderness.

@Rav Mordekhai And do you also reverse the objections raised by one against the other, and do you also reverse that which Rabbi Elazar said, that he saw Rabbi Yoḥanan in a dream and interpreted his opinion to be referring to Reish Lakish instead?
messages.quote: we teach it in the opposite manner

notes.he: ואמריתו ריש לקיש חזאי בחלום ומתריץ ליה למילתיה דריש לקיש והא ר' אלעזר תלמידו דר' יוחנן הוה:
notes.en: And do you also reverse that of Rabbi Elazar: and say “I saw Reish Lakish in a dream,” and he explains Reish Lakish’s statement? But Rabbi Elazar was Rabbi Yoḥanan’s student!

notes.he: דקאמר איתיביה ר"ל לר' יוחנן ואפכיתו נמי להא דר' אלעזר דאמריתו ר"ל חזאי בחלמא:
notes.en: And do you also reverse the objection: where it says “Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yoḥanan”? And do you also reverse that of Rabbi Elazar, so that you say “I saw Reish Lakish in a dream”?

messages.text: @Rav Ashi According to my tradition, when Rabbi Yoḥanan stated that the firstborn in the wilderness were not sanctified he meant that they did not need to be consecrated, i.e., one who wished to sacrifice a firstborn lamb did not need to consecrate it, as they were already sanctified as firstborns. And Reish Lakish disagreed.

notes.he: האי דלא קדשו דקאמר ר' יוחנן היינו דלא הוצרכו לקדש אם רוצה להקריבן אינו צריך להקדישן כשאר בהמות חולין שהרי הן קדושין היו משעה שנולדו דהיינו נמי כדלעיל דלר' יוחנן קדשו בכורות במדבר:
notes.en: He said to him: this “they were not sanctified” that Rabbi Yoḥanan says means that they did not need to be consecrated. If one wishes to sacrifice them, he need not consecrate them as one does other non-sacred animals, for they were sacred from the moment they were born. This is the same as above, that according to Rabbi Yoḥanan the firstborn were sanctified in the wilderness.

notes.he: לא מפכינן דהכי קא משמע לן ללישנא דידן. מאי לא קדשו דאמר ר' יוחנן לא הוצרכו ליקדש בכורות במדבר שהרי קדשו במצרים ולא פסק קדושה לעולם:
notes.en: He said to him: We do not reverse [those], for this is what it teaches us in our version: what is the “they were not sanctified” that Rabbi Yoḥanan said? The firstborn in the wilderness did not need to be sanctified, since they had been sanctified in Egypt and the sanctity never ceased.

messages.text: If so, that is the same as our tradition, that in Rabbi Yoḥanan’s opinion the firstborn that were born in the wilderness were sanctified, and in Reish Lakish’s opinion they were not. For what purpose, then, did Rav Mordekhai inform Rav Ashi of his alternative version of the dispute?
messages.quote: they did not need to be consecrated

messages.text: It teaches us that a person must say what he was taught in the precise language employed by his teacher.

notes.he: אע"ג דתרוייהו כי הדדי הוו פירושייהו אפ"ה קאמר ליה בלשון שלמדתיה:
notes.en: In the language of his teacher: even though both explanations come to the same thing, he nevertheless told it to him in the language in which he had learned it.

notes.he: אין הכי נמי. אלא הא דאפכינן משום דחייב אדם לומר בלשון רבו:
notes.en: If so, that is our version: yes, indeed. But the reason we reversed it is that a person must say [what he learned] in the language of his teacher.

messages.text: @Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai In the individual count of each family of Levites you find that there were 22,300 (see Numbers 3:22–34).
messages.lead: § With regard to the abrogation of the sanctity of the firstborn in the wilderness by the Levites, the Gemara relates:

notes.he: שם שר:
notes.en: Kontrokos: the name of an officer.

notes.he: בגרשון כתיב (במדבר ג׳:כ״ב) שבעת אלפים וחמש מאות ובקהת כתיב (שם) שמונת אלפים ושש מאות הרי ששה עשר אלפים ומאה ובמררי כתיב (שם) ששת אלפים ומאתים הרי שנים ועשרים אלף ושלש מאות ובכללן כתיב (שם) כל זכר מבן חדש ומעלה שנים ועשרים אלף:
notes.en: In the individual count of the Levites: for Gershon it is written (Numbers 3:22) seven thousand five hundred, and for Kehat it is written (3:28) eight thousand six hundred, which makes sixteen thousand one hundred; and for Merari it is written (3:34) six thousand two hundred, which makes twenty-two thousand three hundred. And in their collective count it is written (3:39): “All the males from a month old and upward, twenty-two thousand.”

notes.he: היכא דקא חשיב בני גרשון ובני קהת ובני מררי וכשתצטרף חשבונ' את מוצא כ"ב אלפים וג' מאות:
notes.en: In the individual count of the Levites: where it counts the sons of Gershon, the sons of Kehat and the sons of Merari. When you combine their count, you find 22,300.

messages.text: But in the collective count of the entire tribe you find a total of 22,000, as it is stated: “All the males from a month old and upward, were 22,000” (Numbers 3:39). Where, then, did the other three hundred Levites go?

verse.he: כׇּל־פְּקוּדֵי הַלְוִיִּם אֲשֶׁר פָּקַד מֹשֶׁה וְׄאַׄהֲׄרֹׄןׄ עַל־פִּי יְהֹוָה לְמִשְׁפְּחֹתָם כׇּל־זָכָר מִבֶּן־חֹדֶשׁ וָמַעְלָה שְׁנַיִם וְעֶשְׂרִים אָלֶף׃ {ס}
verse.en: All the Levites who were recorded, whom at GOD’s command Moses and Aaron recorded by their clans, all the males from the age of one month up, came to 22,000.

notes.he: היכא דקא חשיב להו ביחד אינם אלא כ"ב אלפים:
notes.en: And in the collective count: where it counts them together, they are only 22,000.

messages.text: @Kontrokos The total sum includes only those Levites who redeemed the Israelite firstborn. Those additional three hundred Levites were themselves firstborns, and a firstborn Levite cannot abrogate the sanctity of a firstborn Israelite.
messages.quote: In the individual count of each family of Levites you find that there were 22,300

messages.text: What is the reason?
messages.quote: a firstborn Levite cannot abrogate the sanctity of a firstborn Israelite

messages.text: It is sufficient for a Levite firstborn to abrogate his own firstborn sanctity.

notes.he: דיו לבכור לוי שיפקיע קדושת עצמו:
notes.en: It is enough for a Levite firstborn to abrogate his own sanctity.

messages.caption: Kontrokos’s question: the three Levite families add up to 22,300 (Rashi’s sums), but the total is given as 22,000. The three hundred missing were themselves firstborn.

messages.text: With regard to the collection of silver by Moses for the Tabernacle, you find that the total amount is 201 talents and eleven maneh, as it is written that they amassed: “A beka a head, that is, half a shekel, of the shekel of the Sanctuary…for 603,550 men” (Exodus 38:26), which totals 301,775 shekels. This sum equals 201 talents and eleven maneh, as each talent contains 1,500 shekels, or sixty maneh, and each maneh contains twenty-five shekels.

verse.he: בֶּקַע לַגֻּלְגֹּלֶת מַחֲצִית הַשֶּׁקֶל בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ לְכֹל הָעֹבֵר עַל־הַפְּקֻדִים מִבֶּן עֶשְׂרִים שָׁנָה וָמַעְלָה לְשֵׁשׁ־מֵאוֹת אֶלֶף וּשְׁלֹשֶׁת אֲלָפִים וַחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשִּׁים׃
verse.en: a half-shekel. a head, half a shekel by the sanctuary weight, for each one who was entered in the records, from the age of twenty years up, 603,550 men.

notes.he: לגלגלת לשש מאות אלף ושלשת אלפים וחמש מאות וחמשים הרי מאתים ואחד ככר וי"א מנה. ככר הוי ששים מנה ומנה מאה דינר שהן חמשה ועשרים סלעים ושקל דאורייתא הוי סלע. חשוב ס' פעמים כ"ה תמצא בככר אלף וחמש מאות סלעים שהן שלש אלפים חצאי שקלים תמצא לשלש אלפים ישראל ככר כסף לשלש מאות אלף מאת ככר לשש מאות אלף מאתים ככר ולשלשה אלפים אלף וחמש מאות סלעים ולחמש מאות איש ר"ן סלעים ולחמשים איש כ"ה סלעים הרי אלף ות"ש ע"ה סלעים צרף סלעים ועשה מהן מנים מכל מאה סלעים ארבע מנים הרי לאלף סלעים מ' מנים ולחמש מאות סלעים עשרים מנים הרי ככר פשו להו רע"ה סלעים שהן אחת עשרה מנה:
notes.en: Half a shekel, of the shekel of the Sanctuary: per head, for 603,550, which makes 201 talents and eleven maneh. A talent is sixty maneh, and a maneh is a hundred dinars, which are twenty-five sela, and the Torah’s shekel is a sela. Multiply sixty by twenty-five and you find 1,500 sela in a talent, which are 3,000 half-shekels. So for 3,000 Israelites you find a talent of silver; for 300,000, a hundred talents; for 600,000, two hundred talents. For [the remaining] 3,000, 1,500 sela; for 500 men, 250 sela; and for 50 men, 25 sela: that makes 1,775 sela. Combine the sela and make maneh of them, four maneh for every hundred sela: so for 1,000 sela, forty maneh, and for 500 sela, twenty maneh, which makes a talent. There remain 275 sela, which are eleven maneh.

notes.he: כשגבן מכל אחד מחצית השקל וכשתצרפם עולה חשבונם מאתים ואחד ככר ואחד עשרה מנה. כיצד המנה הוא כ"ה שקלים שהוא מאה דינרין. ומאה מחצית שקל הן ב' מנים. נמצא שלשת אלפים מחצית שקל הן ס' מנה שכך הוא ככר של הקדש ס' מנה דילפינן לה מקראי דלקמן דכך הוא הככר מן מאת ככר ומן שבעים ככר. ומזה תוכל להבין כששלשת אלפים עושים ככר אחת כך שלש מאות אלף עושין ק' ככרים ושש מאות אלף מאתים ככרים. והיינו דקאמר מאתים ואחד ככר. וחמש מאות וחמשים מחצית שקלים הן י"א מנה ובנתינת הכסף היכא דעשה חשבון לישראל אי אתה מוצא אלא מאת ככר:
notes.en: In the collection of the silver: when he collected half a shekel from each one, and when you combine them their count comes to 201 talents and eleven maneh. How? The maneh is twenty-five shekels, which is a hundred dinars, and a hundred half-shekels are two maneh. It follows that 3,000 half-shekels are sixty maneh, for that is the talent of the Sanctuary, sixty maneh, as we derive below from the verses, from “a hundred talents” and from “seventy talents.” From this you can understand: as 3,000 make one talent, so 300,000 make a hundred talents and 600,000 two hundred talents. That is why it says 201 talents. And 550 half-shekels are eleven maneh. But in the giving of the silver, where he gave an accounting to Israel, you find only a hundred talents.

messages.text: But with regard to the giving of the silver to the Tabernacle you find only one hundred talents, as it is written: “And the hundred talents of silver were for casting” (Exodus 38:27).

verse.he: וַיְהִי מְאַת כִּכַּר הַכֶּסֶף לָצֶקֶת אֵת אַדְנֵי הַקֹּדֶשׁ וְאֵת אַדְנֵי הַפָּרֹכֶת מְאַת אֲדָנִים לִמְאַת הַכִּכָּר כִּכָּר לָאָדֶן׃
verse.en: The 100 talents of silver were for casting the sockets of the sanctuary and the sockets for the curtain, 100 sockets to the 100 talents, a talent a socket.

messages.text: Now, was Moses your teacher a thief, or was he a gambler [kuveyustus], or was he not expert in accounting? He gave half of the money for the Tabernacle and took half for himself, and he did not return even a complete half to the Tabernacle.

notes.he: שהיה לו לשלם מן החצי מאת ככר וחצי וחמש מנים וחצי והוא לא נתן אלא מאה ככר כדכתיב מאת ככר. ואע"ג דכתיב (שמות ל״ח:כ״ח) ואת האלף ושבע מאות וחמשה ושבעים עשה ווים אלמא דיותר ממחצה החזיר אותו פסוק לא הזכיר אותו השר שמתכוין היה לקנטרו בדברים:
notes.en: And he did not return a complete half: for of the half he should have paid a hundred and a half talents and five and a half maneh, and he gave only a hundred talents, as it is written, “a hundred talents.” And even though it is written, “And of the 1,775 [shekels] he made hooks for the pillars” (Exodus 38:28), which shows that he returned more than half, the officer did not mention that verse, since he intended to provoke him with words.

notes.he: במקום אחר חולין (דף צא:) פרש"י גונב נפשות ואין עניינו כאן גבי גביית כסף ובפרק המוכר פירות (ב"ב דף צב:) גבי עבדים וסתם עבדים אינן גונבי נפשות ור"ח פירש משחק בקוביא והא דאמר בבראשית רבה שלחני נא כי עלה השחר וכי גנב או קוביוסטוס אתה שאתה מתיירא מן השחר דרך משחק בקוביא להטמין עצמו לפי שמפסיד ממון בשחוק ומתחייב בהקפה:
notes.en: Kuveyustus: elsewhere, in Ḥullin (91b), Rashi explained it as a kidnapper; but that meaning does not fit here, where the subject is collecting silver. [Rashi explains it the same way] in the chapter HaMokher Peirot (Bava Batra 92b), with regard to slaves, and ordinary slaves are not kidnappers. Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained it as a dice player. And as for what is said in Bereshit Rabba on “Let me go, for the dawn has broken” (Genesis 32:27), “Are you a thief or a kuveyustus, that you are afraid of the dawn?”: it is the way of a dice player to hide himself, because he loses money at the game and becomes indebted on credit.

notes.he: לא הזכיר לו פסוק ואת האלף ושבע מאות וחמשה ושבעים עשה ווים לעמודים השר לקנטרו נתכוון:
notes.en: And he did not return a complete half: the officer did not mention to him the verse “And of the 1,775 [shekels] he made hooks for the pillars,” since he intended to provoke him.

notes.he: גונב נפש:
notes.en: Or a kuveyustus: a kidnapper.

notes.he: לבזות עצמו נתכוון ומחצה שלם לא החזיר דעדיין חסר חצי מככר האחד וי"א מנה:
notes.en: He intended to disparage him: “and he did not return a complete half,” for half of the one talent and eleven maneh was still lacking.

messages.text: @Kontrokos Moses, our teacher, was a trustworthy treasurer and was expert in accounting, but a maneh of the Sanctuary, which was used to measure the one hundred talents used for the sockets, was double the value of a standard maneh, i.e., fifty shekels instead of twenty-five shekels. Therefore, the one hundred talents given by Moses were equivalent to the two hundred talents that he collected from the Jewish people.
messages.quote: you find only one hundred talents

notes.he: והיה בככר ק"כ מנים ובאותן מאה ככר הוו מאתים ככר והאחד ככר וי"א מנה היו האלף וז' מאות וע"ה שעשה ווים לעמודים:
notes.en: Was double: a talent held 120 maneh, so those hundred talents were two hundred talents, and the one talent and eleven maneh were the 1,775 [shekels] of which he made hooks for the pillars.

notes.he: של מאתים דינר. ומאתים ככר הוו ק' ככר ואחד ככר וי"א מנה כיון שלא היה בהן כדי ככר כפול של קודש לא מנאו הכתוב לא אמר אלא ויהי מאת ככר הכסף והככר וי"א מנה הן אלף שקלים שלמים [ושבע מאות וע"ה] דכתיב ואת האלף וכו':
notes.en: And a maneh of the Sanctuary was double: of two hundred dinars. So two hundred talents are a hundred talents, and the talent and eleven maneh, since they did not amount to a doubled Sanctuary talent, the verse did not count [as a talent]. It said only, “And the hundred talents of silver were,” and the talent and eleven maneh are the full 1,775 shekels, as it is written, “And of the 1,775…”

messages.caption: The half-shekels of 603,550 men, counted twice: in a common maneh of 25 shekels they make 201 talents and eleven maneh; in a Sanctuary maneh of 50 shekels, 100 talents and 1,775 shekels, as Exodus 38:27–28 records.

messages.text: What posed a difficulty for Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai that forced him to offer this answer? Was it the verse: “And the hundred talents of silver were for casting the sockets of the Sanctuary” (Exodus 38:27)? If so, one can explain that these one hundred talents were designated for casting the sockets, and the other one hundred talents that are not mentioned here were placed in the treasury.

notes.he: לרבן יוחנן בן זכאי ומאי דוחקיה דאהדר ליה מנה [של קודש] כפול היה לימא ליה הנך מאת ככר דאמר קרא הוו לצקת ואידך שארא בי גזא הוה מנח:
notes.en: What posed a difficulty: for Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai? What forced him to answer that the [Sanctuary] maneh was double? Let him tell him: those hundred talents of which the verse speaks were for casting, and the rest was placed in the treasury.

messages.text: Another verse is written that discusses the total sum collected, and only one hundred talents are mentioned: “And the silver of those that were numbered of the congregation was a hundred talents” (Exodus 38:25).
messages.quote: and the other one hundred talents that are not mentioned here were placed in the treasury

verse.he: וְכֶסֶף פְּקוּדֵי הָעֵדָה מְאַת כִּכָּר וְאֶלֶף וּשְׁבַע מֵאוֹת וַחֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעִים שֶׁקֶל בְּשֶׁקֶל הַקֹּדֶשׁ׃
verse.en: The silver of those of the community who were recorded came to 100 talents and 1,775 shekels by the sanctuary weight:

notes.he: דלא כתיב ביה לצקת ולא קחשיב לכולהו:
notes.en: Another verse is written: in which “for casting” is not written, and it counts the whole sum.

notes.he: לא הוה יכיל למהדר ליה הכי משום דכתב קרא אחרינא וכסף פקודי העדה מאת ככר ולא כתיב הכא לצקת משום הכי א"ל כפול היה:
notes.en: He could not answer him that way, because another verse is written, “And the silver of those that were numbered of the congregation was a hundred talents,” and “for casting” is not written there. That is why he told him it was double.

messages.text: And with regard to that which Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai said to Kontrokos, that a maneh of the Sanctuary was double the value of a standard maneh, from where does he derive this?
messages.quote: a maneh of the Sanctuary was double

notes.he: פירוש יש לו לדקדק דבר זה מתוך מה אמרה מלבד קושיא זו:
notes.en: From where does he derive this: that is, [the Gemara asks] he should have some source from which to infer this matter, other than this difficulty.

notes.he: דכפול היה:
notes.en: And from where does he derive that it was double?

messages.text: If we say that it is derived from the verse itself that Kontrokos mentioned (Exodus 38:27), then the derivation would be as follows: In addition to the one hundred talents, additional silver coins are mentioned here that equal seventy-one maneh, as it is stated: “And of the 1,775 shekels he made hooks for the pillars” (Exodus 38:28), which is equal to one talent, or sixty maneh, plus an additional eleven maneh, and the verse counted them only using the value of small coins, i.e., shekels, and not in talents.

verse.he: וְאֶת־הָאֶלֶף וּשְׁבַע הַמֵּאוֹת וַחֲמִשָּׁה וְשִׁבְעִים עָשָׂה וָוִים לָעַמּוּדִים וְצִפָּה רָאשֵׁיהֶם וְחִשַּׁק אֹתָם׃
verse.en: And of the 1,775 shekels he made hooks for the posts, overlay for their tops, and bands around them.

notes.he: מהאי קרא גופיה שהרי כיון אלף ושבע מאות וע"ה יוצא שבעים וחד מנה וא"נ לא מהדר אלא כמה דכתיב מיהו הנך הוה ליה לקרא למימני בהו בככר וי"א מנה ולא מנאן אלא בפרוטרוט בפרטי' ולא עשה מהן כלל שיחשבם בככר ש"מ כפול היה:
notes.en: If we say from it: from this verse itself. For since there are 1,775, that comes to seventy-one maneh. And even if he returned only what is written, still the verse should have counted these as a talent and eleven maneh; it did not count them so, but itemized [befrutrot], in their details, and did not make a total of them to reckon them as a talent. Learn from it that [the Sanctuary maneh] was double.

notes.he: ולא מנאן הכתוב אלא בפרוטרוט:
notes.en: Here there are seventy-one maneh: and the verse counted them only in small coins.

notes.he: דההוא קרא וכסף פקודי העדה מאת ככר אלף ושבע מאות (וחמשים) [וחמשה] ושבעים שקל. שהרי כאן שבעים ואחד מנה. כיצד דהכא כתיב שקל דכ"ה שקלים הן מנה ואלף ושבע מאות וחמשה ושבעים שקלים הן שבעים ואחד מנה ולא מנאן הכתוב בככר שהרי יש כאן יותר מככר פשוט של ס' י"א מנה ולא מנאו בככר אלא בפרוטרוט פרוטרוט היינו פרטי כלומר בשקלים מנאן דהיינו פרטי. אלמא משום הכי מנאם בפרוטרוט דלית בהו שעור מנה כפול:
notes.en: If we say from it: from that verse, “And the silver of those that were numbered of the congregation was a hundred talents and 1,775 shekels.” For here there are seventy-one maneh, since twenty-five shekels are a maneh and 1,775 shekels are seventy-one maneh. [The printed text is garbled at this point, and the editor proposes a correction.] The verse did not count them as a talent, even though there is more here than a simple talent of sixty [maneh], [plus] eleven maneh. It did not count them as a talent but itemized; “itemized” [befrutrot] means details, that is, it counted them in shekels, which are details. Evidently it counted them itemized because they did not contain the measure of a doubled [talent].

messages.text: And if it is so that a maneh of the Sanctuary was of equal value to a common maneh, then the verse should have expressed this value using larger coins, writing: 101 talents and eleven maneh.

Rather, since the verse counts this value only using the value of small coins, learn from it that a maneh of the Sanctuary was double the value of a standard maneh and equaled fifty shekels. Therefore, the 1,775 shekels mentioned are worth only 35½ maneh, which is less than a full talent, or sixty maneh.

notes.he: אבל שקלים של חול ושל קדש שוין היו וא"ת מכל מקום למנינהו במנין ולימא ל"ה מנים וחצי וכן בסמוך דקאמר שהרי כאן צ"ו מנים היה לו למנות במנה ולימא ארבעים ושמנה מנים והוי המנים טפי שלם י"ל דמשקל של מנה לא היה עדיין בימי משה ולא משתמיט קרא באורייתא דלכתוב מנה תדע דבפ"ק דכתובות (דף י:) גבי אלמנה אמרי' נקראת אלמנה על שם מנה דעתידי רבנן דמיתקני לה כתובה מנה ומי כתב קרא לעתיד ואמאי לא דייקי' כתובת אלמנה דאורייתא אלא ודאי לפי שלא היה מנה בימי משה:
notes.en: And a maneh of the Sanctuary was double: but common shekels and Sanctuary shekels were equal. And if you ask: in any case, let the verse count them in maneh and say thirty-five and a half maneh; and likewise below, where it says “here there are ninety-six maneh,” it should have counted in maneh and said forty-eight maneh, and the maneh would be a more complete unit. One can answer that the weight of a maneh did not yet exist in Moses’ days, and nowhere does a verse in the Torah write “maneh.” Know that this is so: in the first chapter of Ketubot (10b), regarding a widow, we say she is called almana on account of the maneh, since the Rabbis would in the future institute a ketuba of a maneh for her. Does the verse write [a name] for the future? And why do we not infer [from it] that a widow’s ketuba is by Torah law? Rather, it must be because there was no maneh in Moses’ days.

messages.text: But perhaps the total amount of shekels does equal the amount of a talent, but the verse calculates the general amounts, i.e., the hundreds of talents, in talents, and the verse does not calculate the details, i.e., any amount less than one hundred talents, in talents, but in shekels.

notes.he: לעולם איכא לישאל אמאי לא אהדר מאתים ככר והא דאמרת אי לאו דכפול היה אמאי לא מננהו בככר לאו טעמא הוא דכללי שהגיעו למאה קחשיב בכללי ופרטי כגון חד ככר לא חשיב בככרי לפיכך מנאן בפרוטרוט:
notes.en: In fact one can still ask why he did not return two hundred talents. And as for what you said, that if it was not double, why did the verse not count them in talents: that is no reason, for general sums that reached a hundred it counts in totals, and details, such as one talent, it does not count in talents. Therefore it counted them itemized.

notes.he: אכתי מהכא לא שמעינן דמנה כפול הוה דהאי דלא מני להו הני אלף וז' מאות וע"ה בככר משום דכללי דככרי חשיב ופרטי דככר לא חשיב. כלומר מאה ככר. דמאה היינו כלל חשיב כללי דככרי ככר חד דהיינו פרטא דככרי לא חשיב. ולעולם לאו כפול הוה והאי דלא חשביה בככר משום דלא חשיב פרטי בככרי:
notes.en: But perhaps: we still do not learn from here that the maneh was double. The reason it did not count these 1,775 as a talent is that it counts general sums in talents and does not count details in talents; that is, a hundred talents, since a hundred is a general sum, it counts in talents, but one talent, which is a detail, it does not count in talents. So in fact it was not double, and the reason it did not count it as a talent is that it does not count details in talents.

messages.text: Rather, the principle that a maneh of the Sanctuary is double the value of a common maneh is derived from here: “And the brass of the offering was seventy talents and 2,400 shekels” (Exodus 38:29).

verse.he: וּנְחֹשֶׁת הַתְּנוּפָה שִׁבְעִים כִּכָּר וְאַלְפַּיִם וְאַרְבַּע־מֵאוֹת שָׁקֶל׃
verse.en: The copper from the elevation offering came to 70 talents and 2,400 shekels.

messages.text: Aside from the seventy talents mentioned, there are an additional ninety-six maneh here, which is equivalent to one talent and an additional thirty-six maneh, and the verse counts them only using the value of small coins. Learn from it that a maneh of the Sanctuary was double the amount of a standard maneh, and that is why the number of shekels mentioned did not equal a full talent.

notes.he: אלפים הוו פ' מנים לכל ק' ד' מנים ות' הוו ט"ז מנים הרי צ"ו מנים ולא מנאן אלא בפרוטרוט והאי קרא חשיב פרטי בככרי דהכתיב שבעים ככר מדלא כתב ע"א ככר ושלשים וששה מנים ש"מ כפול היה ועד דליהוו ק"כ מנים לא הוי ככר:
notes.en: And 2,400 shekels: two thousand are eighty maneh, at four maneh for every hundred, and four hundred are sixteen maneh, which makes ninety-six maneh; and it counted them only itemized. Yet this verse does count details in talents, for it writes “seventy talents.” Since it did not write “seventy-one talents and thirty-six maneh,” learn from it that [the maneh] was double, and until there are 120 maneh it is not a talent.

notes.dh: שהרי כאן ליכא כללא דככרי ולא הוה מאה ככר
notes.he: אלא שבעים ככר דהיינו פרטי דככרי והרי יש כאן על שבעים ככר צ"ו מנה דאלף ות' שקל היינו צ"ו מנה ולא מנה אלא בפרוטרוט ואם איתא דככר של הקדש פשוט הוה ע"א ככר ול"ו מנה מיבעי ליה אלא מדמנאן בפרוטרוט בשקל ש"מ דככר כפול הוו ולא הוה בהנהו שקלים שעור ככר כפול:
notes.en: For here there is no general sum of talents: it is not a hundred talents but seventy talents, which are details of talents. And here, beyond the seventy talents, there are ninety-six maneh, for 2,400 shekels are ninety-six maneh, and it counted them only itemized. If the Sanctuary talent were simple, it should have said seventy-one talents and thirty-six maneh. Rather, since it counted them itemized, in shekels, learn from it that the talents were double, and those shekels did not amount to a doubled talent.

messages.text: But perhaps the verse is referring to a standard maneh, and the verse calculates a large unit, i.e., tens of talents, in talents, while the verse does not calculate a small unit, i.e., any amount less than ten talents, in talents.

notes.he: שבעים ולהכי קרי ליה פרט דלא הגיע למאה:
notes.en: A large detail: seventy. It calls it a detail because it did not reach a hundred.

notes.he: כגון חד ככר:
notes.en: A small detail: for example, one talent.

notes.he: לעולם לא הוה כפול והאי דקא חשיב הני בפרוטרוט דאית בהו טפי מככר פשוט משום דפרטא רבא כגון ע' ככר או ס' או נ' או כ' או י' חשיב בככרי אבל פרטא זו א' פחות מי' לא חשיב בככר אלא בפרוטרוט ולעולם נימא דלאו כפול הוא:
notes.en: But perhaps: in fact it was not double. The reason it counts these itemized, though they contain more than a simple talent, is that a large detail, such as seventy talents, or sixty, or fifty, or twenty, or ten, it counts in talents; but a small detail, one, less than ten, it does not count in talents but itemized. So in fact let us say it is not double.

messages.text: The claim that a maneh of the Sanctuary was double the size of a standard maneh is derived from here: “And the shekel shall be twenty gera; twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, ten, and five shekels, shall be your maneh” (Ezekiel 45:12).

verse.he: וְהַשֶּׁקֶל עֶשְׂרִים גֵּרָה עֶשְׂרִים שְׁקָלִים חֲמִשָּׁה וְעֶשְׂרִים שְׁקָלִים עֲשָׂרָה וַחֲמִשָּׁה שֶׁקֶל הַמָּנֶה יִהְיֶה לָכֶם׃
verse.en: And the shekel shall weigh 20 gerahs. 20 shekels, 25 shekels [and] 10 plus 5 shekels shall count with you as a mina. The Mesopotamian mina of 60 shekels; but meaning of Heb. uncertain.

notes.he: פסוק הוא ביחזקאל עשרים שקלים וגו' המנה יהיה לכם. אלמא המנה כ"ה סלעים:
notes.en: And the shekel is twenty gera: it is a verse in Ezekiel: “twenty shekels… shall be your maneh.” Evidently the maneh is twenty-five sela [i.e., the common maneh, one of the verse’s parts].

notes.he: היינו מעין כדמתרגם כ' מעין סלע ותימה האמר סלע ד' דינר ושש מעה כסף דינר אלמא איכא כ"ד מעין בסלע ופר"ת שתי פעמים הוסיפו על המשקל בימי יחזקאל היה שקל עשרים גרה הוסיפו שתות על מנה של קדש שבתחלה היה בו נ' סלעים עשאוהו של קדש ששים אבל על השקל לא הוסיפו ובימי חכמים חזרו והוסיפו על השקל שתות מלבד תוספת שבתחלה שהיה של עשרים ועשאוהו של כ"ד והשתא לפר"ת כשנתוסף בימי יחזקאל נעשה מנה של קדש גדול יותר מכפלים משל חול דשל חול לעולם כ"ה סלעים והם עשו של קדש ס' סלעים ובימי חכמים כשהוסיפו על סלעים ממילא נתוסף מנה של קדש ושל חול וה"פ קרא דיחזקאל והשקל עשרים גרה כלומר מאותם שקלים שהיו בתחלה עשרים גרה יש במנה של עכשיו ששים אבל משקלים של עכשיו שנעשו כ"ד לית ביה אלא חמשים בשל קדש וכ"ה של חול:
notes.en: And the shekel is twenty gera: that is, ma’a, as the Targum renders it, “twenty ma’a to the sela.” And this is puzzling, for it is said that a sela is four dinars and that six silver ma’a are a dinar; evidently there are twenty-four ma’a in a sela. Rabbeinu Tam explained that they added to the weight twice. In Ezekiel’s days, when the shekel was twenty gera, they added a sixth to the Sanctuary maneh, which at first held fifty sela, and made the Sanctuary maneh sixty; but to the shekel they added nothing. Then in the days of the Sages they again added a sixth to the shekel, besides the earlier addition: it had been twenty [ma’a] and they made it twenty-four. So according to Rabbeinu Tam, when the addition was made in Ezekiel’s days the Sanctuary maneh became more than double the common one, since the common maneh is always twenty-five sela and they made the Sanctuary one sixty sela. And in the days of the Sages, when they added to the sela, the Sanctuary maneh and the common maneh both grew automatically. And this is the meaning of Ezekiel’s verse, “And the shekel is twenty gera”: of those shekels that were originally twenty gera there are sixty in the present maneh, but of the present shekels, which became twenty-four [ma’a], it holds only fifty in the Sanctuary maneh and twenty-five in the common one.

notes.he: מהכא והשקל עשרים גרה עשרים שקלים חמשה ועשרים שקלים עשרה וחמשה שקל המנה יהיה לכם חשבון דקרא הוו ס' שקלים וקאמר המנה יהיה לכם כלומר דכך ליהוי מנה:
notes.en: Rather, from here: “And the shekel is twenty gera; twenty shekels, twenty-five shekels, ten and five shekels shall be your maneh.” The verse’s sum is sixty shekels, and it says “shall be your maneh,” meaning that this is how the maneh shall be.

messages.text: In this verse, Ezekiel defines the various weights used in the Temple and states that each silver shekel consists of twenty gera. In addition, the combination of twenty, twenty-five, ten, and five shekels yields a total sum of sixty shekels, which is the value of a maneh. A maneh, in turn, is equivalent to one hundred dinars.

notes.dh: עשרים שקלים חמשה ועשרים שקלים עשרה וחמשה שקל המנה יהיה לכם
notes.he: מה שלא מנה הכתוב בבת אחת ששים שקלים המנה וכן לחלקו בענין זה יש לפרש לפי (דאמרת) שענייני משקלות היו במקדש משקל אחד היה במקדש של עשרים שקלים בה שוקלים שליש מנה של קדש אחר שנתוסף (של קדש) אחד משתות ומשקל אחד של כ"ה שיעור מנה של חול רביע מנה של קדש קודם שנתוסף קדש ומשקלו של ט"ו ושלשתן מחזיקות שיעור מנה של קדש וכן מוכח התרגום דמתרגם וסלעא עשרין מעין תלתות מנה עשרין סלעין מנה דכספא עשרין וחמש סלעים רבעות מנה חמש ועשרה סלעים כולהון שיתין מנה רבא מנה דקודשא יהא לכון ולפי פ"ב אין מתיישב כל כך תלתות מנה רבעות מנה במנה של קודש אחר שנתוסף ומנה דכספא כ"ה סלעים איירי במנה של חול ולא בשל חול אחר שנתוסף אלא במנה של חול מקמי דאיתוסף איירי וא"ת ומנא לן שהוסיף יחזקאל כלום דילמא מתחלה היה מנה של קדש ס' י"ל דמאת ככר של משה מוכיח דתחלתו של קדש לא היה אלא כחול:
notes.en: In brief: Why does Ezekiel not simply say that sixty shekels are the maneh, and why does he divide them as twenty, twenty-five, and ten and five? Because these were the weights kept in the Temple: one weight of twenty shekels, with which they weighed a third of the Sanctuary maneh after the sixth was added; one of twenty-five, the size of a common maneh, [which Tosafot calls] a quarter of the Sanctuary maneh before it was increased; and one of fifteen. The three together make up a Sanctuary maneh. The Targum shows this too, rendering: “The sela is twenty ma’a; a third of a maneh is twenty sela; a maneh of silver is twenty-five sela; a quarter of a maneh is five and ten sela; all of them together are sixty, the great maneh, the Sanctuary maneh, shall it be for you.” On the other explanation, “a third of a maneh” and “a quarter of a maneh” do not fit as well; [the Targum] means the Sanctuary maneh after it was increased, and “a maneh of silver, twenty-five sela” means the common maneh before it was increased. And if you ask how we know that Ezekiel added anything at all, perhaps the Sanctuary maneh was sixty from the start: Moses’ hundred talents prove that originally the Sanctuary maneh was only [double] the common one. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: 5b
But each shekel consists of four dinars, and therefore sixty shekels is equivalent to two hundred and forty dinars, not a maneh, which is generally worth one hundred dinars.

notes.he: בתמיה מאתן וארבעים דנרין הוו ס' שקלים היינו ב' מנים ומאה דנרין:
notes.en: A maneh? [Said] in astonishment: sixty shekels are 240 dinars, which is two maneh and a hundred dinars [so the text; 240 dinars is two maneh and forty dinars].

messages.text: Rather, learn from this verse a number of matters: First, learn that the maneh of the Sanctuary to which Ezekiel was referring was a maneh that was double its standard value. Therefore, it was worth fifty shekels, which is equivalent to two hundred dinars.

notes.he: אלא כפול היה ובמנה דקודש הוו מאתן והנך ארבעים דטפו עלייהו זהו שהוסיפו בימי יחזקאל והוסיפו עליהן שתות דארבעין הוו שתותא מלבר דבמאתן איכא ה' פעמים מ' והביאו פעם מ' ששית מבחוץ והוסיפו עליהן ולא אמרי' שתות מלגיו שיחלקו לששה ויוסיפו על המשקל אחד מאותן חלקים:
notes.en: But they are 240 dinars: rather, it was double, and a Sanctuary maneh held two hundred; and these forty more than that are what they added in Ezekiel’s days. They added a sixth to them, for forty is a sixth from the outside: in two hundred there are five times forty, and they brought another forty, a sixth from the outside, and added it. We do not say a sixth from the inside, that one divides [the original] into six and adds one of those parts to the weight.

messages.text: And furthermore, as Ezekiel stated that the maneh will be sixty dinars, not fifty, learn from it that a community may increase measures, but they may not increase them by more than one-sixth. And learn from it that the one-sixth is calculated from the outside, i.e., it is one-sixth of the final sum, which is one-fifth of the previous sum. Therefore, adding one-fifth of the original fifty shekels, which is ten shekels, to the total equals sixty shekels. It is from this sum that the one-sixth from the outside, ten shekels, is calculated.

notes.he: מדאמר המנה יהיה לכם דמנה של קדש כפול היה. והני ארבעים דהוו טפי ממאתים היינו דהוסיפו על המדה שתות מלבר:
notes.en: Rather, learn from it: since it says “shall be your maneh,” that a Sanctuary maneh was double; and these forty beyond two hundred are what they added to the measure, a sixth from the outside.

messages.text: The Gemara returns to the redemption of firstborn donkeys.
I asked Rabbi Eliezer in the great study hall: In what way are firstborn donkeys different from firstborn horses and camels, i.e., other non-kosher animals, which are not redeemed?

notes.he: בבית המדרש הגדול:
notes.en: In beit motva rabba: in the great study hall.

messages.text: It is a Torah edict. And furthermore, donkeys assisted the Jewish people at the time of their exodus from Egypt, as there was not one member of the Jewish people that did not have ninety Nubian donkeys with him, which were considered to be of superior quality, laden with the silver and gold of the Egyptians.
messages.quote: In what way are firstborn donkeys different from firstborn horses and camels

notes.he: מעולים:
notes.en: Luvim: superior.

notes.he: ע"ש (נחום ג׳:ט׳) פוט ולובים היו בעזרתך ולובים וכושי' במצעדיו חמרא לובאה ר"פ במה בהמה (שבת דף נא:) פירש בערוך חמור מצרי ובירושלמי [גריס] גרים הבאים מפוט ולוב מהו להמתין ג' דורות:
notes.en: Ninety Nubian [luvim] donkeys: named for [Luv, as in] “Put and Lubim were your helpers” (Nahum 3:9) and “and the Lubim and the Kushim shall be at his steps” (Daniel 11:43). The “Luvian donkey” at the beginning of the chapter Bameh Behema (Shabbat 51b) the Arukh explains as an Egyptian donkey. And the Jerusalem Talmud reads: converts who come from Put and Luv, what is the law, must they wait three generations?

messages.text: And furthermore, I also asked Rabbi Eliezer: What is the meaning of the term: “Rephidim,” in the verse: “Then came Amalek, and fought with Israel in Rephidim” (Exodus 17:8)?

verse.en: Amalek came and fought with Israel at Rephidim.

messages.text: that Rephidim was its name, i.e., of the location.
messages.quote: What is the meaning of the term: “Rephidim,”

messages.text: This answer is like one side of a dispute between tanna’im:
Its actual name was Rephidim.

This moniker is an allusion to the fact that the Jewish people became lax [rippu] with regard to the statements of the Torah in Rephidim, and so it says: “The fathers look not back to their children because of feebleness [rifyon] of hands” (Jeremiah 47:3).

verse.he: מִקּוֹל שַׁעֲטַת פַּרְסוֹת אַבִּירָיו מֵרַעַשׁ לְרִכְבּוֹ הֲמוֹן גַּלְגִּלָּיו לֹא־הִפְנוּ אָבוֹת אֶל־בָּנִים מֵרִפְיוֹן יָדָיִם׃
verse.en:
At the clatter of the stamping hoofs of Pharaoh’s stallions,
At the noise of his chariots,
The rumbling of their wheels,
Parents shall not look to their children
Out of sheer helplessness

notes.he: לפיכך בא עליהם עמלק:
notes.en: That they slackened their hands, etc.: and therefore Amalek came upon them.

notes.dh: לא הפנו אבות אל בנים (להציל) מרפיון ידים
notes.he: מכאן שריפו ידיהם מן התורה:
notes.en: The fathers look not back to their children because of feebleness of hands: from here [we learn the word means] that they slackened their hands from the Torah.

messages.text: And furthermore, I also asked him the following question: What is the meaning of the term “Shittim” in the verse: “And Israel dwelled in Shittim” (Numbers 25:1)?

verse.he: וַיֵּשֶׁב יִשְׂרָאֵל בַּשִּׁטִּים וַיָּחֶל הָעָם לִזְנוֹת אֶל־בְּנוֹת מוֹאָב׃
verse.en: While Israel was staying at Shittim, the people profaned themselves by whoring with the Moabite women,

messages.text: that Shittim was its name.
messages.quote: What is the meaning of the term “Shittim”

messages.text: This answer is like one side of a dispute between tanna’im:
Shittim is the actual name of the place.
This moniker is an allusion to the fact that they were engaged in matters of nonsense [shetut], i.e., prostitution and idol worship (see Numbers, chapter 25).

notes.he: לזנות את בנות מואב:
notes.en: In matters of nonsense: to commit harlotry with the daughters of Moab.

messages.text: The same tanna’im also dispute the meaning of another verse discussing that incident. With regard to the verse: “And they called [vatikrena] the people to the offerings of their gods” (Numbers 25:2),

verse.he: וַתִּקְרֶאןָ לָעָם לְזִבְחֵי אֱלֹהֵיהֶן וַיֹּאכַל הָעָם וַיִּשְׁתַּחֲווּ לֵאלֹהֵיהֶן׃
verse.en: who invited the people to the sacrifices for their god. The people partook of them and worshiped that god.

messages.text: Naked women encountered them, which is how they were convinced to engage in idol worship.

notes.he: ותקראן משמע גופן היה פוגע בהן:
notes.en: Naked women encountered them: vatikrena implies that their bodies were encountering them.

notes.he: היו מהלכות ופוגעות בהו בישראל דהיינו ותקראן הן עצמן כלומר בשרן נוגע בהן כדי לבער בהן יצרן:
notes.en: Naked women: were walking about and encountering the Israelites. That is vatikrena: they themselves, that is, their flesh, touched them, in order to inflame their desire.

messages.text: That they all became those who experienced seminal emissions [kerayyin] resulting from the lust they experienced.

notes.he: ולשון מקרה הוא:
notes.en: That they all became ones who experienced emissions: it is the language of mikreh [an occurrence, the term for an emission].

messages.text: Mishna

A cow that gave birth to a donkey of sorts and a donkey that gave birth to a horse of sorts are exempt from their offspring being counted a firstborn, as it is stated: “And every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb” (Exodus 13:13); “and the firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb” (Exodus 34:20).

verse.he: וְכׇל־פֶּטֶר חֲמֹר תִּפְדֶּה בְשֶׂה וְאִם־לֹא תִפְדֶּה וַעֲרַפְתּוֹ וְכֹל בְּכוֹר אָדָם בְּבָנֶיךָ תִּפְדֶּה׃
verse.en: But every firstling donkey you shall redeem with a sheep; if you do not redeem it, you must break its neck. And you must redeem every male first-born among your children.

notes.dh: מתני' פטר חמור פטר חמור שני פעמים
notes.he: כתובים בתורה חד בקדש לי כל בכור (שמות י״ג:ב׳) וחד בראה אתה (שם לד):
notes.en: Mishna. “Firstborn of a donkey,” “firstborn of a donkey,” twice: these are written in the Torah, once in [the passage] “Sanctify to Me every firstborn” (Exodus 13) and once in [the passage] “See, You say to me” (Exodus 33–34).

notes.dh: פטר חמור פטר חמור ב' פעמים
notes.he: א' בסדר בא אל פרעה. וא' בס' כי תשא:
notes.en: “Firstborn of a donkey,” “firstborn of a donkey,” twice: once in the portion Bo el Paro and once in the portion Ki Tisa.

messages.text: The Torah states this halakha twice, indicating that one is not obligated unless both the birth mother is a donkey and the animal born is a donkey.

notes.he: האם:
notes.en: The one that bears: the mother.

notes.he: שהוא דומה לאמו:
notes.en: And the one born is a donkey: that it resembles its mother.

messages.text: And what is the halakhic status of offspring that are unlike the mother animal with regard to their consumption? In the case of a kosher animal that gave birth to a non-kosher animal of sorts, its consumption is permitted. And in the case of a non-kosher animal that gave birth to a kosher animal of sorts, its consumption is prohibited.

notes.he: אותן שאין דומין לאמן:
notes.en: And what is their status with regard to consumption: those that do not resemble their mother.

messages.text: This is because that which emerges from the non-kosher animal is non-kosher and that which emerges from the kosher animal is kosher.
Gemara
With regard to the issue of a kosher animal that gave birth to a donkey of sorts and its firstborn status: We learned in a mishna there (16b):

notes.he: באידך פירקין:
notes.en: We learned there: in the other chapter.

messages.text: A ewe that gave birth to a goat of sorts and a goat that gave birth to a ewe of sorts are exempt from the mitzva of the firstborn. And if the offspring has some of the characteristics of its mother, it is obligated, i.e., subject to the obligations of firstborn status.

notes.he: של אמו:
notes.en: Gemara. Some of the characteristics: of its mother.

messages.text: From where are these matters derived?
messages.quote: are exempt from the mitzva of the firstborn

notes.he: דפטור:
notes.en: From where are these matters derived: that it is exempt.

messages.text: They are derived from a verse, as the verse states with regard to a firstborn kosher animal: “But the firstborn of an ox, or the firstborn of a lamb, or the firstborn of a goat, you shall not redeem, they are holy” (Numbers 18:17).

verse.he: אַךְ בְּכוֹר־שׁוֹר אוֹ־בְכוֹר כֶּשֶׂב אוֹ־בְכוֹר עֵז לֹא תִפְדֶּה קֹדֶשׁ הֵם אֶת־דָּמָם תִּזְרֹק עַל־הַמִּזְבֵּחַ וְאֶת־חֶלְבָּם תַּקְטִיר אִשֶּׁה לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַיהֹוָה׃
verse.en: But the firstlings of cattle, sheep, or goats may not be redeemed; they are consecrated. You shall dash their blood against the altar, and turn their fat into smoke as an offering by fire for a pleasing odor to GOD.

messages.text: The word firstborn seems superfluous in this verse, as it is clear from the context that it is referring to a firstborn. Therefore, the phrase “the firstborn of an ox” is interpreted as teaching that it must be an ox and its firstborn must be an ox in order for firstborn status to apply. Likewise, the phrase “the firstborn of a lamb” teaches that it must be a lamb and its firstborn a lamb, and not another animal. Similarly, the phrase “the firstborn of a goat” teaches that it must be a goat and its firstborn a goat.

notes.he: מדמצי למיכתב אך שור כשב ועז דהא עניינא בבכור קמישתעי דכתיב לעיל מיניה כל פטר רחם וגו' ונקט בכולהו בכור ש"מ עד שיהא הבכור כאמו ולא יהא דומה לאחר:
notes.en: But the firstborn of an ox, etc.: since it could have written “But an ox, a lamb and a goat,” for the passage is speaking of the firstborn, as written just before it, “everything that opens the womb,” etc., and yet it used “firstborn” with each of them, learn from it [that it is not sanctified] unless the firstborn is like its mother and does not resemble another kind.

messages.text: One might have thought that even if the offspring has some of the characteristics of the mother it should still be exempt, as it does not entirely resemble the mother. Therefore, the verse states: “But,” indicating that the Torah makes a distinction with regard to this principle, in that it does not apply when the offspring has some of the characteristics of the mother; and the offspring therefore does have firstborn status.

notes.he: דכל אכין ורקין שבתורה למעט:
notes.en: “But” makes a distinction: for every akh and rak [“but” and “only”] in the Torah comes to exclude.

notes.he: תימה תנא דידן דלית ליה הך דרשא מקצת סימן חייב מנא ליה ומתני' היא פ"ב (לקמן בכורות דף טז:) ולא מיסתבר דפליג אהא דפירקין ומיהו אי לא פליגי קשה דמייתי עלה דתנא כרב יהודה וכי קאמר מה"מ הוה ליה לאיתויי קרא דמתני':
notes.en: The verse states “But,” making a distinction: this is puzzling. Our tanna, who does not have this exposition, from where does he derive that one with some of the characteristics is obligated? That is a mishna in chapter 2 (below, 16b), and it is not reasonable that it disagrees with [the mishna of] our chapter. Yet if they do not disagree, it is difficult that [the Gemara] cites [that mishna] together with a tanna who follows Rav Yehuda; and when it asks “From where are these matters derived?” it should have cited the verse of our mishna.

notes.he: דאם יש בו קצת סימן שדומה לאמו חייב בבכורה וה"ה נמי לתנא דמתנ' דאע"ג דלא קתני ואם יש בו מקצת סימנים דאם יש בו מקצת סימנים דומה לאמו חייב דהכי בעי ליה לקמן איבעיא להו פרה [שילדה] כו':
notes.en: “But” makes a distinction: if it has some characteristic by which it resembles its mother, it is obligated in the firstborn. And the same is true for the tanna of our mishna: even though it does not teach “and if it has some of the characteristics,” if it has some characteristics resembling its mother it is obligated, for so the Gemara asks below: “A dilemma was raised before them: a cow [that gave birth to]…”

messages.text: But doesn’t the tanna of the mishna here cite the verses “firstborn,” “firstborn,” from Exodus (13:13, 34:20), with regard to the case of a cow that gave birth to a donkey of sorts, as teaching that the offspring has no firstborn status? Why, then, does Rav Yehuda resort to interpreting a different verse?
messages.quote: But the firstborn of an ox

notes.he: דמתניתין:
notes.en: But doesn’t the tanna: of our mishna.

notes.he: דקא מפיק פרה שילדה מין חמור דפטורה מן הבכורה מן פטר פטר עד שיהא היולד חמור והולד חמור ופרה נמי גמרה מחמור ורב יהודה היכי שבק קרא דמתניתין וקנסיב למודא אחרינא:
notes.en: Cite “firstborn,” “firstborn” with regard to a cow: for he derives that a cow that gave birth to a donkey of sorts is exempt from the firstborn from “firstborn,” “firstborn”: unless the one that bears is a donkey and the one born is a donkey; and he derives the cow too from the donkey. So how could Rav Yehuda set aside the verse of the mishna and adopt a different derivation?

notes.dh: והא תנא פטר פטר נסיב לה לפרה
notes.he: ואין לומר מ"מ איצטריך קרא דמתני' לפטור מקדושת פטר חמור וקרא דהכא לפטור מדין שור דפטור מן הבכורה דקתני במתני' משמע דלגמרי פטר לה לפרה מכלל דפטר פטר דילפי' מהדדי כדלקמן וא"ת נהי דשמעינן מפטר פטר פרה שילדה מין סוס דילמא ה"מ היכא דאשתני לדבר שאינו קדוש קדושת הגוף אבל כגון רחל שילדה מין עז דקדוש קדושת הגוף הוה אמינא דקדשא וי"ל דמסתבר לגמרי (משמע) דילפינן מהדדי קדושת דמים מקדושת הגוף כדאמר בסמוך וקשה דהא אמר אפילו קדושת הגוף מקדושת הגוף לא ילפי' דהא לשור וכשב ועז צריך קרא לכל חד וחד:
notes.en: But doesn’t the tanna cite “firstborn,” “firstborn” with regard to a cow: one cannot say that in any case the verse of the mishna is needed to exempt [the offspring] from the sanctity of a firstborn donkey, and the verse here to exempt it from the law of an ox. For “exempt from the firstborn,” taught in the mishna, implies that it exempts the cow entirely; this shows that “firstborn,” “firstborn” [and the verse of the ox] are derived from each other, as below. And if you ask: granted, from “firstborn,” “firstborn” we learn [the case of] a cow that gave birth to a horse of sorts [so the text]; perhaps that applies only where it changed into something that has no inherent sanctity, but where, for example, a ewe gave birth to a goat of sorts, which has inherent sanctity, I would say it is sanctified. One can answer that it is entirely reasonable that we derive them from each other, sanctity of value from inherent sanctity, as is said shortly. But this is difficult, for it says that we do not derive even inherent sanctity from inherent sanctity, since for ox, lamb and goat a verse is needed for each one.

notes.dh: והא תנא פטר פטר קא נסיב לה
notes.he: מקשי לרב יהודה מאי שנא דלא יליף לה מפטר פטר מהיכא דיליף תנא דמתניתין אילו הוה משכח בריתא דילפא מאך בכור איכא למימר דרב יהודה סבר לה כוותיה אלא אי מימרא דנפשיה קאמר מאי שנא דלא יליף לה מפטר פטר. אין אשכח ברייתא והוא דקאמר כר' יוסי הגלילי דתניא כו':
notes.en: But doesn’t the tanna cite “firstborn,” “firstborn”: this is asked against Rav Yehuda: why does he not derive it from “firstborn,” “firstborn,” from where the tanna of our mishna derives it? Had he found a baraita that derives it from “But the firstborn,” one could say that Rav Yehuda holds like it; but if he says it as his own statement, why does he not derive it from “firstborn,” “firstborn”? [The answer:] Yes, he found a baraita, and that is why it says “in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, as it is taught…”

messages.text: This interpretation was not suggested originally by Rav Yehuda; rather, he says it in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, as it is taught in a baraita:

notes.he: רב יהודה דאמר כרבי יוסי הגלילי:
notes.en: Rav Yehuda said it in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

messages.text: The phrase “but the firstborn of an ox” indicates that the offspring does not have firstborn status unless it is an ox and its firstborn is an ox. The phrase “the firstborn of a lamb” indicates that the offspring does not have firstborn status unless it is a lamb and its firstborn is a lamb. Likewise, the phrase “or the firstborn of a goat” indicates that the offspring does not have firstborn status unless it is a goat and its firstborn is a goat.

One might have thought that even if the offspring has some of the characteristics of the mother this principle that it must be entirely like the mother applies, and it does not have firstborn status. Therefore, the verse states: “But,” indicating that the Torah makes a distinction with regard to this principle, in that it does not apply when the offspring has some of the characteristics of the mother; and the offspring therefore does have firstborn status.
With regard to what matter do the tanna of the mishna and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili disagree, and therefore derive this halakha from different verses?

notes.he: אמאי יליף תנא מפטר פטר ור' יוסי מאך בכור:
notes.en: With regard to what do they disagree: why does the tanna derive it from “firstborn,” “firstborn,” and Rabbi Yosei from “But the firstborn”?

messages.text: The tanna of our mishna holds that the Merciful One revealed in the Torah that a firstborn donkey, which is subject to sanctity that inheres in its value in that a lamb is given to the priest to redeem it, does not have firstborn status unless it resembles its mother, and the same is true with regard to a kosher firstborn animal, which has inherent sanctity and is sacrificed on the altar.

notes.he: בחמור דקדושת דמים הוא שאינו קדוש [אלא] (בלא) דמיו שיפדהו בשה גלי ביה רחמנא דנדמה פטור וה"ה לבכור בהמה טהורה דקדושת הגוף היא:
notes.en: The Merciful One revealed: with a donkey, which has sanctity of value, since it is sacred only for its value, in that one redeems it with a lamb, the Merciful One revealed that one that resembles [another kind] is exempt; and the same is true for the firstborn of a kosher animal, which has inherent sanctity.

notes.he: גלי רחמנא בקדושת דמים דקילא דבר פדיון הוא פטר חמור דלא קדיש עד שיהא הוא חמור והולד חמור:
notes.en: The tanna of our mishna holds: the Merciful One revealed it with regard to sanctity of value, which is the lighter, since a firstborn donkey can be redeemed, that it is not sanctified unless it is a donkey and its offspring a donkey.

notes.he: כ"ש בקדושת הגוף בכור [בהמה טהורה] דלאו בר פדיה [הוא] דלא קדיש עד שיהא ממש בדמותו [כאמו]:
notes.en: And the same is true: all the more so with inherent sanctity, the firstborn of a kosher animal, which cannot be redeemed, that it is not sanctified unless it is exactly in its likeness [like its mother].

messages.text: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili holds that the Merciful One revealed that a kosher firstborn animal, which is subject to inherent sanctity, does not have firstborn status unless it resembles its mother, and the same is true with regard to a donkey, which has sanctity that inheres in its value, and he derives the halakha of sanctity that inheres in its value from the halakha of inherent sanctity.

notes.dh: ור' יוסי סבר גלי רחמנא בקדושת הגוף
notes.he: וגמר קדושת דמים מקדושת הגוף במה מצינו דלר' יוסי ליכא למימר וה"ה כ"ש דקדושת דמים קילא אלא במה מצינו ובהכי הוו פלוגתייהו דהאי גמר בהו"ה והאי גמר במה מצינו:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yosei holds: the Merciful One revealed it with regard to inherent sanctity, and he derives sanctity of value from inherent sanctity by “just as we found.” For according to Rabbi Yosei one cannot say “and the same is true, all the more so,” since sanctity of value is the lighter; rather, [he derives it] by “just as we found.” And this is their dispute: one derives it by “the same is true” and the other by “just as we found.”

messages.text: And as for the tanna of our mishna, what does he do with this repetition of the word: “Firstborn,” “firstborn,” employed both with regard to an ox and with regard to a lamb and goat, from which Rabbi Yosei HaGelili derives this halakha?

He requires it to teach the halakha of burning the sacrificial portions of the animal on the altar, which is mentioned in this verse: “And you shall make their fat burn” (Numbers 18:17), in accordance with the interpretation of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina.

Why were sacrificial portions stated with regard to a firstborn ox, and the sacrificial portions are mentioned again with regard to a firstborn lamb, and the sacrificial portions are mentioned again with regard to a firstborn goat?
messages.lead: As Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, says:

notes.he: בהאי קרא אך בכור שור או בכור כשב או בכור עז לא תפדה קדש הם ואת דמם תזרוק ואת חלבם תקטיר דכולם אימוריהם קרבים:
notes.en: Why were sacrificial portions stated, etc.: in this verse, “But the firstborn of an ox, or the firstborn of a lamb, or the firstborn of a goat, you shall not redeem; they are holy; you shall sprinkle their blood… and make their fat burn,” [which teaches] that the sacrificial portions of all of them are offered.

notes.dh: למה נאמרו אימורים בבכור שור ואימורים בבכור כבש אימורים בבכור עז
notes.he: דכתיב [בכולהו] ואת דמם (דכולהו) תזרק על המזבח ואת חלבם תקטיר. אמאי איצטריך למיכתב בכולהו ליכתוב אימורין בחד וילפי אידך מיניה:
notes.en: Why were sacrificial portions stated with a firstborn ox, sacrificial portions with a firstborn lamb, sacrificial portions with a firstborn goat: for it is written of all of them, “you shall sprinkle their blood on the altar and make their fat burn.” Why was it necessary to write it of all of them? Let it write the sacrificial portions with one, and derive the others from it.

messages.text: It is necessary, as had the Merciful One written the halakha of burning the sacrificial portions on the altar only with regard to a firstborn ox, one might have said only an ox’s sacrificial portions are burned, as an ox offering has more wine libations than a lamb or a goat. Therefore, perhaps the additional obligation of burning the sacrificial portions applies only to an ox.
messages.quote: Why were sacrificial portions stated with regard to a firstborn ox

notes.he: נסכיו מרובים חצי ההין וכשב ועז רביעית ההין. כשב אלייתו קריבה עם אימורים כדמפרש בויקרא מה שאין כן בשור ועז:
notes.en: An ox: its libations are greater, half a hin, while a lamb and a goat have a quarter of a hin. A lamb: its tail is offered with the sacrificial portions, as is explained in Leviticus, which is not so for an ox and a goat.

notes.he: למיכתב בכולהו. הנך לא אתי משור שכן שור נתרבה בנסכים דאית ליה חצי הין לפר. ואי כתב אימורין בכבש אידך לא ילפי מיניה דיש בכבש מה שאין בשור ועז שכן כשב נתרבה באליה:
notes.en: They are necessary: to write it with all of them. These cannot be derived from an ox, since an ox has more libations, half a hin for a bull. And had it written the sacrificial portions with a lamb, the others could not be derived from it, since a lamb has something that an ox and a goat lack: a lamb has more with its tail.

messages.text: Likewise, if this halakha had been written only with regard to a lamb, one might have thought only a lamb’s portions are burned, as it has more sacrificial portions than other animals because its tail is also included.

Likewise, if it had been written only with regard to a goat, one might have thought the burning of the portions applies only in that case, as it has an increased applicability with regard to the case of an individual guilty of idol worship, who brings a goat as a sin offering; unlike one who commits other sins unwittingly, for which a lamb may be brought.
The halakha with regard to one of these cases, i.e., an ox, lamb, or goat offering, evidently cannot be derived from one of the others. Why not derive one of them from the other two?

With regard to which case shall the Torah not write this halakha? If the Merciful One shall not write it with regard to an ox, and one should derive it from these other cases, that derivation is not valid. What is notable about these offerings, i.e., a lamb and a goat? They are notable in that they have an increased applicability with regard to the Paschal offering, for which a lamb or a goat is suitable but not an ox.

notes.he: כשב ועז פסח בא מהן דכתיב מן הכבשים ומן העזים תקחו:
notes.en: A lamb and a goat: the Paschal offering comes from them, as it is written: “You shall take it from the sheep or from the goats” (Exodus 12:5).

notes.dh: מחדא לא אתו תרווייהו אלא תיתי חד מתרתי
notes.he: מה להנך כשב ועז דין הוא שנתרבו לאימורין שכן נתרבו אצל פסח שפסח בא מהם:
notes.en: Both cannot be derived from one, but let one be derived from two: what about these, a lamb and a goat? It is reasonable that they have more with regard to sacrificial portions, since they have more with regard to the Paschal offering, which comes from them.

messages.text: If the Merciful One should not write this halakha with regard to a lamb, and one should derive it from these cases of an ox and a goat, that derivation is not valid either. What is notable about these offerings, i.e., an ox and a goat? They are notable in that they have an increased applicability with regard to a case where the entire Jewish community is guilty of unwitting idol worship, as in such a case the community brings an ox as a burnt offering and a goat as a sin offering (see Numbers 15:24), but not a lamb.

notes.dh: שור ועז נתרבו אצל עבודת כוכבים בציבור
notes.he: פר לעולה ושעיר לחטאת:
notes.en: An ox and a goat have an increase with regard to the community’s idol worship: a bull for a burnt offering and a goat for a sin offering.

notes.he: שור ועז שכן נתרבו אצל (פסחים עז) [עבודת כוכבים] בצבור דמביאין פר ושעיר אבל לא כבש:
notes.en: What about these: an ox and a goat, which have more with regard to communal idol worship, since a bull and a goat are brought, but not a lamb.

messages.text: If the Merciful One shall not write the obligation to burn the sacrificial portions with regard to a goat, and one should derive it from these cases of an ox and a lamb, that derivation is not valid either. What is notable about these offerings, namely, an ox and a lamb? They are notable in that they have an element of increase with regard to the altar, as the libations for an ox are larger than those for a goat; and also the tail of a lamb, but not that of a goat, is a sacrificial portion.

notes.dh: שור וכשב יש בהן צד ריבוי אצל מזבח
notes.he: דכשהן קרבים יש מהן לאשים יותר מעז שור בנסכים וכשב באליה:
notes.en: An ox and a lamb have an element of increase with regard to the altar: when they are offered, more of them goes to the fires than of a goat: the ox in its libations, and the lamb in its tail.

notes.he: שור וכשב שכן (יכול) [יש] בהן צד ריבוי אצל מזבח שור בנסכים וכשב באליה אבל עז אין בו צד רבוי למזבח:
notes.en: What about these: an ox and a lamb, which have an element of increase with regard to the altar: an ox in libations and a lamb in its tail. But a goat has no element of increase for the altar.

messages.text: Therefore, all three cases are necessary.

notes.he: הילכך איצטריך למכתב דמם וחלבם דמשמע אכולהו:
notes.en: Therefore it was necessary to write “their blood” and “their fat,” which refer to all of them.

messages.text: And how does Rabbi Yosei HaGelili interpret this verse as teaching that a firstborn must resemble its mother in order to have firstborn status? Isn’t the verse necessary to teach the halakha of burning the sacrificial portions upon the altar?

If it is so that the verse teaches only that halakha, let the verse write: But a firstborn ox, lamb, or goat. Why do I need the word “firstborn” to be repeated with regard to a lamb, and the word “firstborn” to be repeated again with regard to a goat?

notes.he: דלא אתיא קרא אלא להכי:
notes.en: If so: that the verse comes only for this.

notes.dh: ורבי יוסי הגלילי אם כן ליכתוב קרא אך בכור שור וכשב ועז
notes.he: והא דדרשינן מינה עד שיהא שור ובכורו שור אע"ג דאיצטריך לכדר' יוסי בר חנינא משום דכעין בכור שני ושלישי יש לנו לדרוש מן הראשון:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: if so, let the verse write “But a firstborn ox, lamb and goat”: and the reason we expound from it “unless it is an ox and its firstborn an ox,” even though [the first “firstborn”] is needed for the teaching of Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Ḥanina, is that, like the second and third “firstborn,” we should expound the first as well.

notes.he: דמפיק האי קרא לעד שיהא הוא שור ובכורו שור (א"כ דלהאי דרשא דר' חנינא לחוד אתא) א"כ. דלהכי לחוד אתא דאמור' בכור שור כשב [ועז קריבין] ליכתוב קרא אך בכור שור כשב ועז ובהכי סגיא לאימורין בכור בכור למה לי כו':
notes.en: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili: who derives from this verse “unless it is an ox and its firstborn an ox.” If so, that it comes only for this, that the sacrificial portions of a firstborn ox, lamb [and goat are offered], let the verse write “But a firstborn ox, lamb and goat,” and that would suffice for the sacrificial portions. Why do I need “firstborn,” “firstborn”? …

messages.text: Rather, isn’t it correct to conclude from here that the mother is not subject to having its offspring counted as a firstborn unless it resembles its mother, e.g., the mother is an ox and its firstborn is an ox?

notes.he: תרווייהו נפקי מיניה:
notes.en: Learn from it: both are derived from it.

messages.text: And as for Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, what does he do with this phrase: “Firstborn of a donkey,” “firstborn of a donkey,” mentioned twice in Exodus, from which the tanna of the mishna derives that the offspring must resemble its mother in order to have firstborn status?
He requires that phrase for that which is taught in a baraita:

Since it is stated: “Yet you shall redeem the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of non-kosher animals you shall redeem” (Numbers 18:15), I would derive that even firstborn horses and camels must be redeemed, as they too are non-kosher animals. Therefore, the verse states: “Firstborn of a donkey,” which indicates I said to you that firstborn status applies to a firstborn donkey, but not to firstborn horses or camels.

verse.he: כׇּל־פֶּטֶר רֶחֶם לְכׇל־בָּשָׂר אֲשֶׁר־יַקְרִיבוּ לַיהֹוָה בָּאָדָם וּבַבְּהֵמָה יִהְיֶה־לָּךְ אַךְ ׀ פָּדֹה תִפְדֶּה אֵת בְּכוֹר הָאָדָם וְאֵת בְּכוֹר־הַבְּהֵמָה הַטְּמֵאָה תִּפְדֶּה׃
verse.en: The first [male] issue of the womb of every being, human or animal, that is offered to GOD, shall be yours; but you shall have the first-born of human beings redeemed, and you shall also have the firstling of impure animals redeemed.

messages.text: And still I can say that the phrase “firstborn of a donkey” merely indicates that firstborn donkeys alone are redeemed by means of a lamb, while firstborn horses and camels are redeemed by means of any other item.

notes.dh: ועדיין אני אומר פטר חמור תפדה בשה
notes.he: ולא בדבר אחר ושאר בכורי טמאה בכל דבר ולעולם קדושים בבכורה:
notes.en: And still I say: a firstborn donkey you shall redeem with a lamb and not with anything else, while other firstborn non-kosher animals are redeemed with anything, and they are in fact sanctified as firstborn.

messages.text: Rabbi Yosei HaGelili’s baraita continues on 6a: that is why “firstborn of a donkey” is stated twice.
